main_body: Half-timbered house: a large red-tile hip roof (rows 0-43) over a plaster and timber front wall (rows 44-107) with windows, flower boxes, a door and hanging signs
top_band: Red/orange tile roof slope from row ~2 to ~43 with lighter highlight tiles at the ridge and left hip, ending in a dark eave edge at rows 42-43
evidence: Reading a column through the middle, the tiled roof slope is a large foreshortened surface (hip planes at the left and right, chimney on the slope). It ends in a dark eave line at rows 42-43, then a shaded band of plaster under the eave at rows 44-47, then the vertical timber and plaster wall. Windows have sills and flower boxes, and the door is inset between posts. The roof reads as a real top surface like the references, so this is a proper 3/4 building.

style.evidence: The roof has per-tile scallops with 5 or more tones (highlight, orange, red, maroon, deep) and the same warm tile ramp as the references. Outlines are dark brown and dark maroon, tinted to the adjacent material rather than black. The plaster is speckled, the timber has grain and shadow, and the windows, flower boxes, signs, awning and door add many colours per tile. It is at least as rich as the references and has no large flat fills.
